topic.definition: Drift is what happens when a description and the thing it describes stop agreeing: the written record still says one thing while the code has quietly moved on. s0ma turns that disagreement into something a machine can notice. Every generated document carries a fingerprint of everything it was built from, and recomputing that fingerprint says at once whether the two still match.
topic.do_not_use_when: Drift is not a word for a document that is badly written, out of date in its judgement, or missing a section. Those are editorial problems and a fingerprint cannot see them. Drift is the narrow, mechanical case where the source a document was built from has changed and the document has not been rebuilt.
topic.purpose: Drift is the failure the whole product exists to prevent. Naming it, fingerprinting it, and rechecking it on every merge is what turns "the documentation is accurate" from a claim somebody makes into a fact the build can prove.
topic.summary: The gap that opens when a written description and the thing it describes stop agreeing.
topic.use_when: Ask for the drift check whenever you need to know whether the written record still matches the system: before a release, in the merge gate, and after any change to something a document describes.
